styles.label: Balanced
styles.thesis: The tuned us54 baseline every other style is read against

styles.label: Blitz
styles.thesis: Tempo and sets now; information is cheap
styles.rationale: RULES_US54 row 9 — a hit keeps the turn, so tempo compounds

styles.label: Punter
styles.thesis: Chase the completing card; accept the gift risk
styles.rationale: RULES_US54 row 14 — a wrong declare gifts the set, a 2-point swing

styles.label: Banker
styles.thesis: Never gift a set; bank only certainties
styles.rationale: RULES_US54 row 14 — the gift is the whole cost model

styles.label: Turtle
styles.thesis: Minimum risk; declare only sets wholly in hand
styles.rationale: STYLES.md §3.1 — the stall risk, gated by avgMoves

styles.label: Hoarder
styles.rationale: RULES_US54 row 6 — holding a card is the licence to ask into that set

styles.label: Scout
styles.rationale: RULES_US54 row 17 — the public log is the whole information channel

styles.label: Ghost
styles.rationale: RULES_US54 row 17 — every ask leaks; Ghost prices the leak

styles.label: Archivist
styles.thesis: Track sets you hold nothing in, and declare them for teammates
styles.rationale: RULES_US54 row 15 — declaring without holding is legal and now live

criteria.label: highest mean score
criteria.detail: balanced at 0.5935, ahead of blitz at 0.5554 (margin 0.0381)

criteria.label: maximin > 0.5 (no losing matchup)
criteria.detail: maximin 0.5336 vs blitz, CI95 lower bound 0.5240 > 0.5; worst cell is significant after BH

criteria.label: exploitability not materially worse than rivals'
criteria.detail: E(balanced) = 0.0554 vs rivals' median 0.1093 (margin 0.0200); not materially worse

ranking.verdictSummary: No dominant style. The matrix is cyclic (energy 0.0700, 1 significant 3-cycle(s)); criteria (3) fail. Publish the counter-graph and the Nash mixture, not a winner.

replays.caption: Blitz (seats 0/2/4) against Banker (seats 1/3/5) on one seeded us54 deal. Every declare in the log resolves to one team or the other — row 14 abolished the void, so no set is ever burned. This single deal clinched 2–5 to banker with 2 set(s) unresolved. One game is an anecdote: the cell it belongs to, with 2,600 duplicate pairs behind it, is on /lab/matrix.

The back-edge of the highlighted cycle — Hoarder against Blitz — played out once from seat 3. This single deal clinched 1–5 to blitz with 3 set(s) unresolved. One game is an anecdote: the cell it belongs to, with 2,600 duplicate pairs behind it, is on /lab/matrix.
